newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SWEET CRUDE GRADES RECOVER, SOUR PRICES SOFT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SWEET CRUDE GRADES RECOVER, SOUR PRICES SOFT.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf faltered Wednesday afternoon on carryover selling from a stressed gasoline market and bearish sentiment ahead of Iraq returning to world oil export markets, traders said.
At 1503 EDT (1903 GMT), September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ranged around the NYMEX screen at $20.45-55 a barrel, down some 30 cents from Tuesday's close.
Grade barrels recovered somewhat for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James, which sold at a low of 13 cents over September WTI, but now talked around 15-20 cents over marker.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold between $1.48 and $1.50 under WTI/Cushing, declining on the scramble for barrels before Iraq starts to pitch oil sales, likely from Friday.
The U.N. Sanctions Committee has until 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT) Friday to offer objections to Iraq's pricing formula, which was recommended for adoption on Wednesday morning by U.N. oil overseers.

Once the so-called "no-objection" procedure expires Friday, Iraq can start submitting oil contracts to the overseers. U.N. sources do not expect any delays in the process, but markets were pondering what immediate impact the return of Iraq would have on prices.
